title: Centralizers of maximal split tori in a minimal rational parabolic
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field] and let $G$ be a reductive $k$-group [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]: smooth, affine of finite type and geometrically connected, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup after extension to an algebraic closure. Unipotent means admitting a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation in which all geometric points are unipotent matrices. A split torus is a group scheme isomorphic over $k$ to $\mathbf G_{m,k}^r$, $r\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units. A parabolic $k$-subgroup $P\subseteq G$ means a smooth geometrically connected closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose fppf right-coset sheaf $G/P$ is represented by a proper finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Here the coset sheaf is the sheafification of $A\mapsto G(A)/P(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras, and $G(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}A,G)$. A minimal parabolic is one containing no strictly smaller parabolic $k$-subgroup; proper means $P\ne G$. Let $P$ be a minimal parabolic of $G$ and let $S_1,S_2\subseteq P$ be closed split tori maximal under inclusion among closed split tori of $P$. For $S\subseteq G$ define $C_G(S)(A)$ to consist of the $g\in G(A)$ such that for every commutative $A$-algebra $B$ and every $s\in S(B)$ the elements $g_B,s$ commute. The functors $C_G(S_i)$ are represented by reductive closed $k$-subgroups $L_i\subseteq P$. Let $U=R_uP$ be the largest smooth geometrically connected normal unipotent $k$-subgroup of $P$. Multiplication gives isomorphisms $U\rtimes L_i\xrightarrow{\sim}P$, where the action is conjugation and the underlying scheme is $U\times_kL_i$. There exists $u\in U(k)$ with $uL_1u^{-1}=L_2$ as subgroup schemes. This statement includes $P=G$ when $G$ has no proper parabolic. No perfectness or infinitude assumption is made on $k$.

source.place: Theorem 25.6(b),(c), printed pp.545--546, restricted to minimal parabolics. The missing minimality hypothesis in (b) is confirmed by the author errata, https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iagerrata.html, entry p.545 et seq. The same restriction makes (c) usable here. Only existence of the conjugator is asserted.

proof.text: For each $i\in\{1,2\}$ apply [lem-sfb-parabolic-prescribed-split-cocharacter] to $P$ and its given maximal split torus $S_i$. This supplies $\lambda_i^0:\mathbf G_m\to S_i$ with $P=P_{\lambda_i^0}$, as equality of the limit functors on all algebra-valued points. This application uses maximality inside $P$ exactly as assumed; it does not require that $S_i$ already be known maximal in $G$.

source.place: Theorem 25.1 and the cocharacter choice in 25.6(b), pp.544,546.

proof.text: Fix $i$, write $S=S_i$ and $\lambda^0=\lambda_i^0$, and choose a closed faithful embedding $G\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(V)$ by [lem-sfb-affine-group-faithful-linear-representation]. By [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition], choose a basis with $S$-characters $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_n$ (repetitions allowed). Use [lem-sfb-split-torus-hom-matrices] to identify characters and cocharacters of $S\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ with integral exponent vectors and their usual pairing. Choose an integral vector $\mu$ nonorthogonal to each nonzero difference $\chi_a-\chi_b$: substituting $(1,M,\ldots,M^{r-1})$ into each of the finitely many nonzero integral linear forms excludes only finitely many integers $M$. For $r=0$ there are no such differences and take $\mu=0$. Put $\lambda_i=N\lambda^0+\mu$ for a positive integer $N$ larger than every $|\langle\chi_a-\chi_b,\mu\rangle|$. Each nonzero pairing with $\lambda^0$ retains its sign, and each nonzero difference has nonzero pairing with $\lambda_i$. This is an integral choice, so no supply of rational field elements is needed.

source.place: Lemma 13.51, p.274, finite weight separation; explicit large-N perturbation retaining the original chamber signs.

proof.text:
In that basis conjugation of a matrix entry $g_{ab}$ by a cocharacter $
u$ multiplies it by $t^{\langle\chi_a-\chi_b,
uangle}$. Over any $k$-algebra $A$, extension to $A[t]$ is equivalent to $g_{ab}=0$ for each negative exponent. The determinant stays the original invertible constant. Such an extension lies in the closed subgroup $G$: every defining equation vanishes after Laurent restriction, and $A[t]\hookrightarrow A[t,t^{-1}]$ is injective. The sign preservation in step 2 therefore gives $P_{\lambda_i}\subseteq P_{\lambda_i^0}=P$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry], $P_{\lambda_i}$ is parabolic, so minimality of $P$ makes this inclusion equality. Commutation with $\lambda_i$ forces $g_{ab}=0$ whenever its exponent is nonzero, by comparing Laurent coefficients over $A$. Step 2 makes those exactly the pairs with $\chi_a
e\chi_b$. These are also exactly the equations for commuting with $S_i$: the monomials for distinct characters are distinct basis elements of $A[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$. Thus $C_G(S_i)=Z_{\lambda_i}$ as functors, including on nonreduced test algebras. In what follows write $L_i=Z_{\lambda_i}$.

source.place: Theorem 13.33(b) proof, pp.265--266 (matrix equations and intersection with a faithful embedding); 13.51, p.274; corrected 25.6(b), p.546.

proof.text: The cocharacter geometry node gives represented smooth geometrically connected closed groups $L_i=Z_{\lambda_i}$ and $V_i=U_{\lambda_i}$, a retraction $r_i:P\to L_i$ with kernel $V_i$, a split-unipotent series for $V_i$, and the multiplication isomorphism $V_i\rtimes L_i\simeq P$. After extension to $\bar k$, the same node identifies $L_{i,\bar k}$ with the centralizer of $\lambda_{i,\bar k}$; the matrix equations of step 3 identify it also with $C_{G_{\bar k}}(S_{i,\bar k})$. Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-fixed-subgroup] over the algebraically closed field $\bar k$: $G_{\bar k}$ is reductive by hypothesis and $S_{i,\bar k}$ is a torus. This makes $L_{i,\bar k}$ reductive. Unipotence of $V_i$ in the item's sense is read off in $G\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(V)$: order the basis of step 2 by decreasing $\langle\chi_a,\lambda_i\rangle$. By the entry formula of step 3, a point $g\in V_i(A)$ has $g_{ab}=0$ when $\langle\chi_a-\chi_b,\lambda_i\rangle<0$ and $g_{ab}=\delta_{ab}$ when it is $0$, so $g$ is block upper unitriangular and $(g-I)^n=0$. Together with smoothness, affineness, finite type and geometric connectedness already obtained, this is exactly reductivity of $L_i$ in the item.

source.place: Corollary 17.59, printed p.371 (the all-field consequence of 17.57); Theorem 13.33 and 25.6(b).

proof.text: We verify that $V_i$ is the specified radical $U$, rather than just an arbitrary normal unipotent subgroup. Let $N\subseteq P$ be any smooth geometrically connected normal unipotent $k$-subgroup. Over $F=\bar k$, factor $r_{i,F}|_{N_F}$ by [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image] into a faithfully flat map onto a closed image $I\subseteq L_{i,F}$. The map $r_{i,F}:P_F\to L_{i,F}$ itself is faithfully flat: under $P_F\simeq V_{i,F}\times L_{i,F}$ its coordinate map is $F[L_i]\to F[V_i]\otimes_F F[L_i]$, and tensoring with a nonzero vector space is exact and detects zero. Thus [lem-sfb-unipotent-normal-quotient-image] applies to this map and $N_F$, and says $I$ is smooth connected normal and unipotent. Reductivity of $L_{i,F}$ forces $I=1$. Hence $N_F\subseteq V_{i,F}$. This inclusion descends to $k$: every defining equation of $V_i$ pulls back to a function on $N$ whose tensor with $F$ is zero, so the function was zero, since a field extension is faithful on vector spaces. Conversely $V_i$ is smooth geometrically connected normal unipotent by step 4. It is therefore the largest such subgroup, so $V_1=U=V_2$. The two multiplication isomorphisms of step 4 are exactly $U\rtimes L_i\simeq P$.

source.place: Proposition 17.60 proof, printed p.372: the reductive quotient identifies the cocharacter kernel with the unipotent radical; explicit image and descent argument.

proof.text:
Factor $\lambda_1:\mathbf G_m	o P$ through its faithfully flat image $T\subseteq P$ by [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image]. By [lem-sfb-field-split-torus-flat-quotient], $T$ is a split torus. Factor $r_2|_T$ the same way through a closed image $D\subseteq L_2$, again a split torus by that quotient node. Under $P\simeq Utimes L_2$ the inverse image $H=r_2^{-1}(D)$ is exactly $Utimes D$, with conjugation action. It is closed, and $T\subseteq H$ because $r_2|_T$ factors through $D$. Each member of the series of $U$ from step 4 is smooth, connected and contains the rational identity point, so is geometrically connected by [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected]; with the unipotence of step 4, $U$ is split unipotent as the absorption lemma requires. Apply [lem-sfb-split-unipotent-torus-absorption] to this $U$, the split torus $D$ and this $T$. It gives $u\in U(k)$ such that $uTu^{-1}\subseteq D\subseteq L_2$. Consequently $
u=\operatorname{Int}(u)\circ\lambda_1$ factors through $L_2$. Conjugating the all-algebra limit and commuting formulas gives $P_
u=uPu^{-1}=P$ (since $u\in P(k)$) and $C_G(
u)=uL_1u^{-1}$. Write the latter reductive group as $M$.

source.place: Proposition 16.54, printed p.344, in place of the bare Springer reference in 25.6(c); explicit split-solvable reduction.

proof.text:
Since $L_2=C_G(\lambda_2)$, the cocharacters $
u$ and $\lambda_2$ commute on all test algebras. Thus $\lambda_2$ factors through $M=C_G(
u)$ as well. We show $M=L_2$ using the cocharacter geometry and the weight decomposition. In a reductive closed subgroup $J\subseteq G$ containing a cocharacter $\eta$, if $J\subseteq P_\eta$, then $P^J_\eta=J$: the extended orbit stays in $J$ because its defining equations vanish in $A[t,t^{-1}]$ and hence in $A[t]$. Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-cocharacter-parabolic-geometry] to the reductive group $J$. Its $U^J_\eta$ is smooth geometrically connected and normal in $P^J_\eta=J$; it is unipotent because, in a basis of $V$ splitting $V$ into $\eta$-weights by [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition] (rank one), the argument of step 4 makes its points block upper unitriangular. Thus it is a smooth geometrically connected normal unipotent subgroup of $J$, so is trivial by reductivity after $ ar k$ and faithful scalar extension. The same node gives $J=Z^J_\eta$, so $J$ centralizes $\eta$. Use this argument first with $(J,\eta)=(M,\lambda_2)$: here $M\subseteq P=P_{\lambda_2}$ and $\lambda_2$ factors through $M$, giving $M\subseteq L_2$. Then use $(J,\eta)=(L_2,
u)$: here $L_2\subseteq P=P_
u$ and $
u$ factors through $L_2$, giving $L_2\subseteq M$. Hence $uL_1u^{-1}=M=L_2$. No dimension or rational-point-density inference is used.

source.place: Theorem 13.33(b), pp.265--266; the reductive P(lambda)=G argument of Proposition 25.2, printed p.545, applied twice to the two Levi subgroups.

proof.text: All constructions and inclusions above are over $k$ and on every algebra-valued test, so the equalities are subgroup-scheme equalities and the conjugator is the single rational point $u\in U(k)$ of step 6. The empty character-difference set and the zero cocharacter were allowed in steps 1--3. In particular the argument includes $P=G$ when it is minimal; then $U=1$ by reductivity and the same argument gives $L_1=L_2=G$. No step uses infinitude or perfectness of $k$.

source.place: Endpoint and rank-zero checks for the preceding argument.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q126-430abcfc1 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes and all ten cited statements in full, plus Milne iAG pp.544–546 (25.1, 25.2, 25.6, 25.8–25.10) and p.344 (16.54). Statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from live; this is not a re-split. The item is true with the minimality correction (the GL_2, P=G counterexample to printed 25.6(b) checks). Steps 1–8 are mathematically correct: the weight perturbation keeps the signs, minimality gives P_{λ_i}=P, C_G(S_i)=Z_{λ_i} holds on nonreduced test algebras, the k̄-only lemmas are used only after base change, the radical's maximality is proved, the step-6 absorption is valid, and the step-7 double-centralizer argument holds. New node prescribed-split-cocharacter is true.
